articles.title: Two Different Kinds of Gamma-Ray Bursts Erupted 4 Minutes Apart. Astronomers Have Never Seen This Before.
articles.description: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most energetic cosmic events since the Big Bang, releasing the most energetic type of radiation, gamma rays – the stuff that turned unassuming Bruce Banner into the rampaging Hulk, but on an astronomical, potentially plan…
articles.summary: Astronomers observed two different types of gamma-ray bursts erupting just 4 minutes apart—an unprecedented discovery about some of the universe's most energetic events. This rare occurrence promises new insights into cosmic explosions dating back to the Big Bang.

articles.title: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope Captures Eerie Cat’s Head
articles.description: Intricate structures within the Cat’s Head Nebula are illuminated in this mid-infrared view from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope released on Oct. 29, 2026. The distinctive “cat’s head” shape of the nebula was likely sculpted over time by the intense ultraviolet radiation and winds from massive stars in the Carina Nebula. As this stellar feedback […]
articles.summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope reveals stunning mid-infrared details of intricate structures within the Cat's Head Nebula, showcasing stellar nursery complexity.

articles.title: Ghostly Cat’s Head Nebula lurks within sight of Hubble and Webb
articles.description: The NASA/ESA Hubble and the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescopes recently stared at an eerie star-forming scene within the Carina Nebula, a massive gas and dust cloud located approximately 7500 light-years away from Earth. The two telescopes offer complementary views of the shadowy form, nicknamed the Cat’s Head Nebula, which reflects the 'magical'' process of star formation. Hubble’s visible-light view shows the cat as a dark, elongated dust pillar and hints of young forming stars, while Webb’s infrared-light imagery unveils many stars and other hidden details.
articles.summary: The Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes collaborate to reveal the haunting beauty of the Cat's Head Nebula, a dynamic star-forming region.

articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: Japan's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission successfully launches toward Phobos, marking an exciting chapter in Mars system exploration.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo, the joint ESA-JAXA Mercury mission launched in 2018, celebrates its anniversary with continued success on its groundbreaking journey.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope discovers its first previously unknown comet, demonstrating the mission's exceptional observational capabilities.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: ESA's Solar Orbiter has directly observed magnetic switchbacks in the solar wind, mysterious S-shaped kinks that help us understand solar physics and space weather phenomena.

articles.title: Hera Probe Sees Asteroid Pair Separately for First Time
articles.description: Planetary defense is a growing concern among the scientific community, as efforts have been made to design and implement missions meant to deflect incoming threats to the Earth well in advance. In 2022, NASA intentionally collided the Double Asteroid Redirection test (DART) planetary defense spacecraft into the smaller asteroid of the binary asteroid, Didymos and Dimorphos, with the latter being the smaller one. While the goal was to ascertain if deflecting an asteroid is feasible, how did this influence the geological characteristics of Dimorphos, and what can it teach us about planetary defense missions?
articles.summary: NASA's Hera probe has achieved the first separate imaging of a binary asteroid pair, advancing planetary defense capabilities and asteroid characterization science.

articles.title: This Ancient Meteorite Hints at Mars' Warm, Wet Past
articles.description: Ancient Martian meteorites are like time-capsules from the planet's past. They're delivered to us by impacts that launch them into space, where some of them find their way to Earth. One recently discovered meteorite found in the Sahara desert adds weight to the idea that Mars was once warm and wet, and possibly habitable.
articles.summary: Ancient Martian meteorites provide compelling evidence of Mars' warm, wet ancient past, offering insights into planetary habitability and evolution.

articles.title: It's a Ghost! No, It's a Stellar Crèche!
articles.description: Astronomers using the Chandra X-ray Observatory (CXO), the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) zeroed in on a wispy-looking region of the Carina Nebula and found a ghostly looking cloud seemingly floating in isolation among the other clouds of gas and dust. Just in time for Hallowe'en, although, it turns out that little cloud isn't the soul of departed stars. Instead, it's a region of the nebula has been actively engaged in creating batches of hot, young new stars.
articles.summary: Chandra X-ray Observatory and JWST jointly resolved a wispy cosmic structure, revealing it to be a stellar nursery with extraordinary detail and clarity.

articles.title: Tiny photonic chip links telescopes together to view the universe in 'astonishing' detail
articles.description: A tiny glass chip developed by researchers at Heriot-Watt University has linked two telescopes together to enable them to act as a single powerful instrument, marking an important step toward a new generation of astronomical technology.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: A revolutionary photonic chip developed at Heriot-Watt University has successfully linked telescopes to achieve unprecedented imaging resolution of the cosmos.

articles.title: JWST reveals a distant galaxy that may let most of its ionizing radiation escape
articles.description: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) have found evidence that a distant, exceptionally blue galaxy may allow most of its ionizing radiation to escape into space. Known as EBG-1, the gravitationally lensed galaxy is seen at a redshift of 9.244, about 530 million years after the Big Bang. The paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 16.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: JWST has discovered a distant blue galaxy that efficiently leaks ionizing radiation, providing new understanding of how early galaxies shaped the universe's ionization history.

articles.title: NASA's TRACERS first results offer peek into violent magnetic process
articles.description: NASA's TRACERS (Tandem Reconnection and Cusp Electrodynamics Reconnaissance Satellites) mission has gathered its first clues to how space weather affects Earth's magnetic field. In a new paper published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Space Physics, researchers break down how these interactions work after analyzing initial observations from the first year of the mission.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA's TRACERS mission has begun revealing data about violent magnetic reconnection processes in Earth's magnetosphere. This groundbreaking research helps scientists understand fundamental plasma physics phenomena.

articles.title: Scientists smash oxygen nuclei to recreate matter from the Big Bang
articles.description: Scientists have recreated a primordial state of matter from the dawn of the universe by colliding oxygen nuclei at nearly the speed of light. The surprising results show that this exotic substance can form in smaller, lower-energy collisions than previously demonstrated, challenging the known boundaries of early-universe physics.
articles.summary: Scientists have successfully recreated primordial matter from the Big Bang by colliding oxygen nuclei at near-light speeds. This experimental achievement provides direct insights into the universe's earliest moments.

articles.title: Hubble reveals a stunning twist in how the universe emerged from darkness
articles.description: A surprising discovery by astronomers using the Hubble Space Telescope is challenging a leading explanation for how the early universe emerged from a dense fog of hydrogen roughly 13 billion years ago. Scientists once believed powerful winds from exploding stars helped radiation escape galaxies and clear that cosmic fog, but new observations reveal that these winds actually block radiation instead.
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope has revealed surprising new insights into how the universe emerged from its dark ages, challenging existing theoretical models. This discovery opens new avenues for understanding cosmic evolution.

articles.title: Physicists created a tiny universe and watched time emerge without a clock
articles.description: Scientists have created a miniature universe in the laboratory that could help answer one of the biggest mysteries in physics: What is time, and where does it come from? Using 24,000 ultracold atoms, a University of Birmingham researcher built an isolated quantum system that repeatedly expands and contracts, mimicking the Big Bang and a possible Big Crunch. Remarkably, the experiment showed that time could emerge from changes happening inside the system, without relying on an external clock.
articles.summary: Physicists have created a miniature universe in the laboratory that demonstrates how time can emerge without conventional clocks. This groundbreaking experiment may help solve fundamental mysteries about the nature of time itself.

articles.title: Einstein's equations may explain the universe without dark energy
articles.description: Mathematicians have uncovered what they argue is a fundamental flaw in the standard model of the universe, potentially challenging the need for dark energy. Their calculations suggest that the mathematical framework used to describe cosmic expansion is inherently unstable and that the universe could accelerate naturally under Einstein's original theory of gravity. The findings also raise surprising questions about whether our location in the universe is as ordinary as scientists have long assumed.
articles.summary: Mathematicians have identified potential flaws in the standard model and propose that Einstein's equations alone may explain the universe without dark energy. This theoretical breakthrough could revolutionize cosmological understanding.

articles.title: A mysterious star system just 16 light-years away may be hiding habitable planets
articles.description: Astronomers have solved a 170-year-old planetary mystery in a nearby two-star system, discovering that a mysterious wobble was caused by stellar activity rather than a giant planet. Although Jupiter-sized worlds have been ruled out in key regions, smaller, potentially habitable planets could still be waiting to be discovered just 16 light-years from Earth.
articles.summary: Astronomers have solved a 170-year-old mystery in a nearby star system just 16 light-years away, discovering potentially habitable planets. This exciting finding brings the search for life closer to home.

articles.title: Figuring out where cosmic neutrinos come from is tricky - radio telescopes could help find where these ‘ghost particles’ originate
articles.description: A researcher just won a Nobel Prize for detecting tiny particles from space. Scientists now want to get better at figuring out where in the cosmos they come from.
articles.summary: Scientists are using radio telescopes to better understand the origins of cosmic neutrinos, building on a Nobel Prize-winning detection breakthrough. Advanced technology may unlock mysteries of these elusive 'ghost particles' from space.

articles.title: Possible dwarf planet discovered beyond Pluto
articles.description: Astronomers have found a large icy object beyond Pluto, dubbed 2026 ED138, that could become the solar system’s sixth dwarf planet Read Full Article at RT.com
articles.summary: Astronomers discovered a large icy object beyond Pluto designated 2026 ED138, which could become the solar system's sixth dwarf planet. This discovery expands our understanding of the outer solar system's distant regions.

articles.title: Rubin Observatory Spots Possible Dwarf Planet Beyond Pluto—the Biggest in 20 Years
articles.description: The distant, icy celestial body could be our solar system's sixth dwarf planet.
articles.summary: The Rubin Observatory discovered a possible dwarf planet beyond Pluto—the largest such find in 20 years—marking a major breakthrough early in its survey mission. This distant, icy body could reshape our understanding of the solar system's outer reaches.

articles.title: Giant new dwarf planet discovered in our own solar system — hiding in plain sight
articles.description: A large object in the Kuiper Belt — a distant region of icy and rocky bodies past Neptune — appears to be a new candidate dwarf planet.
articles.summary: A large object in the Kuiper Belt has been identified as a new dwarf planet candidate, hiding in plain sight within our own solar system. This discovery highlights how much remains to be learned about our cosmic neighborhood.

articles.title: The Rubin Observatory Finds Its First Dwarf Planet Candidate
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory found a distant Solar System object before its decade-long Legacy Survey of Space and Time even got started. The object is a dwarf planet candidate named 2026 ED138, and if confirmed, it will be one of the largest dwarf planets beyo…
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory achieved a landmark discovery of its first dwarf planet candidate before officially beginning its decade-long survey mission. This success demonstrates the observatory's remarkable potential for future discoveries.

articles.title: Astronomers Discover a Giant New Dwarf Planet Candidate Hiding Beyond Pluto
articles.description: What else could be out there?ScienceAlert stories are written, fact-checked, and edited by humans, never generated by AI. Don't miss a story, subscribe here.
articles.summary: Astronomers discovered a giant new dwarf planet candidate beyond Pluto, sparking wonder about what other discoveries await in the outer solar system. Each find expands the possibilities of what exists in the distant reaches of space.

articles.title: A small star is eating a brown dwarf so slowly that the meal could last billions of years, and the two orbit each other every 87 minutes inside a space that would fit within the Sun
articles.description: A small red star is pulling gas from a brown dwarf as the pair circles every 87 minutes, packed into an orbit that could fit inside the Sun. Material strikes the star’s surface and lights up a hot spot, marking a meal that could continue for billions of years…
articles.summary: A red star and brown dwarf form an extraordinary binary system where the star slowly consumes its companion over billions of years while orbiting every 87 minutes. This extreme cosmic partnership showcases the universe's most exotic gravitational dances.

articles.title: A drive to remember
articles.description: Perseverance’s record-breaking drive distance is in the spotlight. Plus, Hera is getting close enough to spy its two tiny targets.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover set a record-breaking drive distance on Mars while the Hera mission approaches its targets to study asteroid deflection. These achievements showcase humanity's expanding capabilities in planetary exploration.

articles.title: NASA Explores Potential Commercial Servicing for Hubble Telescope
articles.description: NASA issued a Request for Information Oct. 29 to learn more about industry capabilities for in-space servicing to support the agency’s Hubble Space Telescope.
articles.summary: NASA seeks industry partnerships to develop commercial in-space servicing capabilities for the iconic Hubble Space Telescope, extending its scientific mission.

articles.title: November’s Night Sky Notes: Light-Day Away
articles.description: Twin Travelers In 1977, NASA launched twin spacecraft Voyager 1 and 2, taking advantage of a once-every-175-year planetary alignment of the four largest planets in our solar system: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Using six gravity assists between them, this Grand Tour gave us up-close views of the gas and ice giants, including several moons. […]
articles.summary: A November sky guide celebrates the historic 1977 Voyager 1 and 2 missions and their remarkable journey through the solar system's outer reaches.

articles.title: Map Showing Potential Origins of Martian Meteorite Teghaza 001
articles.description: Description This global map of Mars shows 13 locations that match the mineralogy and chemistry of Teghaza 001, one of the most ancient Martian meteorites ever found on Earth. While scientists can never know for sure where a Martian meteorite originated, Teghaza 001 includes clues that link it to highlands in the southern hemisphere of […]
articles.summary: Scientists map 13 potential Martian locations matching the mineralogy of meteorite Teghaza 001, advancing understanding of Mars's geological history.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: Japan's Martian Moons eXploration mission is scheduled to launch on an H3 rocket, beginning an ambitious exploration of Mars's moons.
